extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent agents/attorneys), USPTO discipline/compliance staff, and legal ethics advisors
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, regulatory violations, remedial requirements, and procedural sanctions applied to a USPTO-registered patent practitioner for mishandling client funds, recordkeeping failures, and submitting checks drawn on insufficient funds. Covers required remediation, reporting, and publication of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a separate identifiable bank account for client funds (37 C.F.R. §10.112(a) & (b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Must maintain a separate identifiable bank account (client trust account) into which client funds, including monies received as payment in advance for patent law services to be provided in the future, are deposited; client funds must not be deposited in a business/operating account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order notes Respondent maintained a business/operating account but did not have a separate account for unearned client funds and deposited client funds into the business account. The remedial requirement: establish a client trust account in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §10.112(a) and (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separately preserve the identity of client and business funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Client and business funds must be kept distinct and their identities separately preserved; commingling is prohibited under 37 C.F.R. §10.112(a) & (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent was found to have failed to separately preserve the identity of client and business funds. The Order requires establishing procedures (trust account, ledgers, software) to ensure separation and identity preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain complete accounting records for client funds (37 C.F.R. §10.112(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep complete, accurate accounting records for client funds; failure to maintain complete records violates 37 C.F.R. §10.112(c)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent admitted he did not keep complete accounting records. The remedial plan includes using a manual ledger, acquiring financial software capable of client trust functions, converting transactions to the new system, and monthly reconciliations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit checks that are returned for insufficient funds (37 C.F.R. §§10.23(b)(4) & 10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not sign/submit checks that are drawn on accounts having insufficient funds; submitting checks that are returned for insufficient funds violates 37 C.F.R. §§10.23(b)(4) and 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent signed and submitted nine checks returned for insufficient funds (total $4,677.00) between Nov. 2005 and Jan. 2009. The Order required Respondent to make good on outstanding checks and untimely payment fees and to ensure future checks are not returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a client trust account and implement proper accounting systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a client trust account in accordance with the regulations and implement accounting systems (manual ledger and/or financial software) capable of performing proper client trust account functions; convert all new clients and transactions to the new system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent established a Client Trust account, is using a manual ledger on CPA recommendation, acquired financial software capable of trust-account functions, and is converting existing clients/transactions to the new system as part of remedial compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete a legal ethics course on client trust account management
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete continuing education/legal ethics training specifically on client trust account management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent completed a legal ethics course on client trust account management; the Order lists completion of such a course as a stipulated remedial measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage a certified public accountant (CPA) to assist practice management
rubrics_metrics.description: Hire a CPA to assist in improving practice management, specifically financial bookkeeping, bank arrangements, and implementation of systems to ensure compliance with client trust account rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CPA's role per the Order includes recommending a manual ledger, financial software, reviewing fee/engagement letters, setting up checklists and reconciliation schedules, and preparing periodic compliance reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use fee/engagement and closing letters reviewed by professional advisers
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize fee/engagement and closing letters that have been reviewed by a CPA and other attorneys to ensure clarity and compliance with practice/accounting procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent implemented new fee/engagement and closing letters reviewed by the accountant and other Texas attorneys as part of practice improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement document tasks, policies, and checklists with reconciliation deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute checklists and procedures for financial reporting and USPTO transactional procedures, including required reconciliations of trust and operating accounts by specified monthly deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent set up checklists requiring monthly reconciliation of trust and operating accounts and other procedural checklists to prevent recurrence of failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA periodic reporting at 6, 12, 18, and 24 months identifying compliance and specific failures
rubrics_metrics.description: At Respondent's expense, the CPA must prepare and submit reports to the OED Director at six, 12, 18 and 24 months indicating whether (a) client funds are maintained in a client trust account (not business/personal accounts) and (b) no checks from the trust or operating account were returned for insufficient funds; reports must identify each transaction of noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must specifically identify each transaction where Respondent failed to maintain client funds in the trust account or issued a check that was subsequently returned. Deadlines may be extended only by written agreement of Respondent and the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation with stayed suspension contingent on compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may be suspended (e.g., twenty-four months) but have that suspension stayed while serving a probationary period (e.g., twenty-four months); permission to practice continues unless the stay is lifted for noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's 24-month suspension was stayed and he was placed on 24-month probation; if OED believes Respondent failed to comply, OED will issue an Order to Show Cause with 15 days to respond and may seek immediate lifting of the stay and suspension up to 24 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural protections and timelines for Order to Show Cause
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED believes a practitioner failed to comply during probation, the practitioner is issued an Order to Show Cause, sent to the address of record, and granted fifteen (15) days to respond; thereafter OED may forward materials to the USPTO Director to lift the stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order describes the exact process: OED issues Order to Show Cause; sends to respondent's last address of record per 37 C.F.R. §11.11(a); grants 15 days to respond; if OED remains of that opinion, OED may request the Director lift the stay and impose suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish public notice of discipline (OED Reading Room and Official Gazette) and provide reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director must publish the Final Order in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and publish a Notice of Stayed Suspension in the Official Gazette, giving public notice of the discipline and the reasons therefor pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes sample Notice of Stayed Suspension text describing the violations and remedies, and mandates posting at http://des.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp and publication in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the disciplinary record in future proceedings as aggravating factor or rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of the disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, shall be considered in addressing further complaints of the same or similar misconduct and may be used (a) as an aggravating factor in determining future discipline and/or (b) to rebut any representation by or on behalf of the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly states the record may be consulted in future complaints or disciplinary proceedings and used accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement and procedural authority requirements (37 C.F.R. §11.26; 35 U.S.C. §2(b)(2)(D))
rubrics_metrics.description: Settlement agreements resolving disciplinary complaints must satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. §11.26 and are authorized by statutory and regulatory provisions (e.g., 35 U.S.C. §2(b)(2)(D)), with the Director or designate approving settlements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This action is the result of a settlement agreement pursuant to the cited statutes/regulations; the Final Order records the stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions required under those provisions.
